ordered_diagnoses: Surgical complication - morcellation-related dissemination of malignant cells

facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient has a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex, with biopsy results showing poorly differentiated epithelioid cells and grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
The patient has multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, with biopsy results showing poorly differentiated epithelioid cells and grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
The patient has a history of superficial pelvic endometriosis, which was noted and cauterized during surgery.

concepts.preferred_label: Surgical complication - morcellation-related dissemination of malignant cells
concepts.why: The patient underwent prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag, which may have led to the dissemination of malignant cells.

rationales.F05: Prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag may have disseminated malignant cells.
rationales.F06: Superficial pelvic endometriosis is a known risk factor for endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F10: Multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest suggest disseminated disease.
rationales.F11: Poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis are characteristic of high-grade malignancy.
rationales.F12: Grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma is a high-grade malignancy with a high risk of dissemination.

frontier_selector.rationale: Multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, along with poorly differentiated epithelioid cells and grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma, support disseminated endometrioid adenocarcinoma, and the history of morcellation without a containment bag provides a plausible mechanism for dissemination.
